001_N: Eleven forty-one at night. You stand at a stranger's door, out of breath.
005_HERO: Let me in. We have eleven minutes for two.
002_N: Above you, a twenty-nine is blinking. Not counted yet. Above the one who opened the door, too.
003_TEMA: What's up? You ran across the whole district.
004_N: In nineteen minutes both counters turn to zero. To stop that, you need eleven.
006_N: What if a counter of days hung over you, and one missed day burned it?
008_N: Day one. You stand at a door with a sign that says Boxing, pretending for the third time that you're just passing by.
009_N: You have exactly one reason: you're tired of flinching when someone raises a hand fast.
010_N: You walk in. And a one lights up over your head.
012_N: You look around. Numbers hang over everyone who trains here.
013_N: The old man with the jump rope: fourteen hundred. The girl at the bag: two hundred twelve.
014_N: Big Vovan: forty-one. He's proud of it and stands so everyone can see.
015_TRAINER: New guy? Wraps first. The hand is made of small bones.
016_N: Wraps hold the small bones of your hand. So they don't break on your very first bag.
017_TRAINER: Group enrollment in thirty-three days. Three are for sickness.
018_TRAINER: I take only those with thirty over their heads.
019_N: Nobody explains the counter rules. Everyone knows only the main one.
020_N: Miss a day, and at midnight it burns to zero. And everyone sees it.
021_N: Next to you, a guy in red is tangled in his wraps. He has a one, too.
022_TEMA: Tyoma. First day, too. Can you help? I got tangled.
024_TRAINER: Jump rope. Ten minutes. That's boxing, too.
025_N: At exactly seven thirty p.m., Tyoma grabs his bag and runs. Without saying goodbye.
026_N: Day three. Everything hurts. Even muscles you didn't know you had.
027_N: Muscles hurt most one to three days after a workout. You're right at the peak.
028_N: Evening. No strength for the gym. You decide stretching on a mat counts as training.
029_N: You google what the counter counts. The internet offers you a pedometer.
030_N: A small heart appears next to the tag for the first time. Gray. Eighty beats a minute.
031_N: Eleven forty-five. The tag blinks red.
032_HERO: What?! But I stretched! Twenty minutes!
033_N: The counter doesn't need a checkmark. It needs work. The heart has to pound.
034_N: Kitchen. Jump rope. Three rounds of three minutes, like at the gym. A timer on your phone.
035_N: The heart turns red: one-twenty, one-forty, one-fifty.
036_N: Mom appears in the doorway. Looks at you. Looks at the chandelier. Leaves without a word.
038_N: Rule one. Effort counts. Not a checkmark, not noise, but how your heart beats.
039_N: For the next week you and Tyoma test the counter like scientists. Your lab is the yard behind the garages.
040_TEMA: Experiment one. How much does it take to count?
041_N: One round, and at night the tag blinks. Two rounds, it still blinks.
042_TEMA: Writing it down: fewer than three doesn't count. Moving science forward.
044_N: Every time, you finish what's missing before midnight. Checking is scary.
045_N: Three rounds of three minutes with a minute of rest, and it glows green. That's how adult amateurs fight.
046_TEMA: Experiment two. No bag, no pads.
047_N: Shadowboxing in the yard. Heart one-fifty. Counted. The place doesn't matter.
048_N: Experiment three happens by accident. In the middle of round two, Tyoma's mom calls.
050_N: Thirty seconds of talking. The heart fades. And that round burns.
051_N: You stopped, so start the round over. The counter sees every pause.
053_TEMA: Let's just run. Running is easier.
054_N: Ten minutes of steady running. The heart is yellow, one twenty-five. Not counted. The pulse doesn't reach.
056_HERO: For the counter, yes. For your legs, no.
057_N: Rule two. Three rounds. No stopping. The place doesn't matter. Steady running doesn't count.
058_N: And again seven thirty, and Tyoma runs off. Every day, at the same time.
059_N: Where do you think he goes? We'll come back to it.
061_N: Your arms are the same as a week ago. But the punches are faster and more accurate.
062_N: In the first weeks, strength grows mostly because the brain learns to switch the muscles on. The muscles catch up later.
063_N: Day twelve. Smack, and the coach nods for the first time.
064_N: Day fifteen. In the morning the thermometer shows thirty-eight point two.
065_N: You drag yourself to the gym anyway. In a scarf, with a red nose and a blinking fifteen over your head.
066_TRAINER: With a fever, go home. Right now.
068_TRAINER: If it burns, you start over. You've got one head.
069_N: Midnight. The counter doesn't burn. It turns gray. A small word on top: pause.
070_N: Three days of gray pause. Tyoma's too: you caught a cold together, in the yard. You recover, and it's fifteen again.
071_N: For all three days you check the gray tag every half hour. Like a thermometer.
072_N: And Vovan decided he'd found a loophole.
073_N: He texts the coach: sick. And goes to the movies.
074_N: Midnight. His forty-one doesn't turn gray. It burns. To zero.
075_N: By morning the photo of his zero is already in the gym's group chat.
076_N: Rule three. Illness freezes the counter. Lying burns it. And the counter knows the difference.
077_N: Day eighteen. Seven thirty. Tyoma runs off again. This time you follow.
078_N: Tyoma isn't going for a walk. He's running home. At the entrance his mom waits in scrubs.
079_N: She's leaving for a night shift at the hospital. And Tyoma stays with his little brother. Until morning.
080_TEMA: What are you doing here? Were you following me?
082_TEMA: What's there to say? It's not laziness. It just happened.
083_HERO: I thought you were just slacking.
085_N: Mom is alone. Hospital at night, sleeping in the day. Around eight the door closes behind Tyoma until morning.
086_TEMA: Gym until nine. And I have to run at seven thirty.
087_HERO: Then let's do it here. Under the window. I'll hold the pads.
088_N: Three rounds under the window. The brother watches from above and counts the punches out loud.
089_N: At twenty-nine the brother loses count and starts over. Nobody minds.
090_N: In the middle of round two Tyoma's shoelace comes undone. The knot pulls tight. Tyoma fights with it for almost a minute.
091_N: And all that time you keep moving with the pads, not standing for a second. And somehow Tyoma's heart doesn't fade.
092_N: Midnight. You're home, looking at your tag. Green. Though today you never threw a punch yourself.
093_N: Strange. They counted both. Even Tyoma with the shoelace.
094_N: Day twenty-two. Two tests in a row. You come home and sit down for a minute.
095_N: You open your eyes. Eleven forty-one.
097_N: The apartment sleeps. You dash onto the stairs. Three rounds of shadowboxing between floors.
098_N: You count the seconds in a whisper, so you don't wake the neighbors. The heart pounds louder than you.
100_N: The next day you tell it at the gym. The old man with the jump rope silently draws in the air with a finger: zero zero, zero two.
101_N: Once he finished two minutes after midnight. And everything burned. Since then, fourteen hundred.
102_N: Rule four. Don't start before midnight. Finish.
103_N: Day twenty-nine. Tomorrow is thirty, and with it the tournament group. Today is your sister's concert.
104_N: Mom's on shift. There's no dad. You're the one going to the concert. You promised a month ago.
105_N: Your sister sings off key and loud. You clap louder than anyone.
106_N: The concert runs seven to nine. The gym closes at nine. You choose the concert.
107_N: Then you sit with your sister until Mom is back. Like Tyoma. Only for you it's one evening.
108_N: Eleven o'clock. Mom's home. You wrap your hands. Eleven minutes, and the counter is saved.
109_N: Eleven oh two. You call Tyoma to do the rounds at the same time, like last week.
110_TEMA: My brother has thirty-eight and a half.
111_TEMA: Mom said: a cool towel every two minutes.
112_TEMA: I started twice. Every two minutes, stop.
114_N: Illness freezes the counter. But it's the brother who's sick, not Tyoma. His twenty-eight days will burn.
116_N: First: your own rounds at home, until eleven sixteen. Your counter is saved.
117_N: Then a run to Tyoma. Thirty-six minutes. You're at his door at eleven fifty-two.
118_N: Tyoma starts at fifty-five and finishes at six past midnight. After midnight. Zero.
119_N: Second path: run right now. But your own rounds aren't done yet.
120_HERO: Finish at home, and that's it?
121_N: You tear off the wraps. And run out.
122_N: The buses don't run anymore. Five kilometers of steady running. You can't go faster.
123_N: Eleven twenty-three. Halfway. Your legs are like cotton, but you keep a steady pace.
124_N: Heart: one-thirty. Yellow. Running doesn't count, you tested it yourself in the yard.
125_N: Eleven thirty. How do you fit two elevens into eleven minutes?
127_N: Eleven forty-one. A stranger's door. You can't catch your breath. Now you know why you ran.
128_HERO: Let me in. We'll do them together.
129_TEMA: You could've done it all at home.
130_HERO: I could. Let me in, it's time.
131_N: Eleven forty-four. A basin by the bed. A stack of towels. Pads wrapped so they don't slap. The brother sleeps two steps away.
132_N: One rule against you: stop, and the round burns. But in a pair, the round goes on while at least one of you works.
133_HERO: Tap, don't hit. Quietly. When I change the towel, you don't stop.
136_N: Round one. Light taps, almost no sound. But footwork, slips, tempo. Both hearts turn red.
137_N: Eleven forty-six. You step to the bed. Fifteen seconds. Tyoma punches the air and doesn't stop.
138_N: Eleven forty-seven. Rest. At eleven forty-seven thirty, a fresh towel while you rest.
139_N: Round two. Eleven fifty. Tyoma goes to his brother. And you work with empty pads: duck, step, duck.
140_N: Eleven fifty-one. Rest. At fifty-one thirty, a towel again. Round three. The last one.
141_N: Eleven fifty-four. You're at the bed again. The brother opens his eyes and looks at you.
142_N: Eleven fifty-five. The timer hits zero. You slide down the wall.
143_N: The brother stands in the doorway. With a towel on his forehead.
144_TEMA: When you get better. I promise.
145_N: Midnight. The twenty-nine over both of you stops blinking.
146_N: The next day, thirty. The coach writes two names on the board.
148_N: Day forty-one. You're wiped out. Nine p.m., you sit on the bed, and that's it.
149_N: Midnight. Forty days in a row turn into zero.
150_N: By morning the photo of your zero is already in the group chat. You lie there staring at the ceiling.
151_N: On the fridge hangs your sister's card: "Forty days for Sanya!" She drew it yesterday.
152_N: Forty days. To zero. Why even get up?
154_N: Your legs carry you to the gym. By themselves. You don't remember lacing up.
155_N: At the gym, Vovan. The one whose forty-one burned at the movies.
156_N: Above him, twenty-nine. He wraps his hands without looking. Like brushing teeth.
157_HERO: You burned. Why did you come?
158_N: Vovan shrugs and points at his sneakers. As if to say, they did it themselves.
159_N: He didn't start over out of grief. He just kept coming.
160_TRAINER: Scientists looked for the moment when you do it on autopilot.
161_TRAINER: For a typical person, sixty-six. One missed day changed almost nothing.
162_N: That's a study from University College London. The spread is from eighteen to two hundred fifty-four days.
163_N: A habit didn't form in people who missed often. And one missed day barely touched it.
164_N: And this is about habit. Showing up without talking yourself into it. How you punch is a different score.
165_N: The tag over you blinks. And changes. Now it shows not days in a row, but habit.
166_N: Zero was never the end. The counter was just counting the wrong thing.
167_N: Day sixty-six. Your bar is almost full. Tyoma's is shorter. Everyone has their own time.
168_TEMA: Looks like mine is all two hundred fifty-four.
169_HERO: Then I'll come with you for all two hundred fifty-four.
170_N: The coach no longer looks at the tags. He looks at where your elbows are.
172_N: Evening. Tyoma's mom is on shift again. In the yard under the window, three shadows.
173_N: Over the smallest one, a one lights up.
174_N: And you? What did you quit after your first miss? Be honest.
175_N: In a month, a tournament. And that same evening, Tyoma's mom has a night shift again.
